words.en: whose valour was destroyed by the sprinkling of water from (her) water-pot
words.g: m. acc. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); predicate accusative with अकरोत्, qualifying शत्रून्
m. acc. pl. of the bahuvrīhi stem हतौजस् (see Samāsa); a second predicate accusative with शत्रून्
f. nom. sg. of ब्रह्माणी (feminine of ब्रह्मन्, ‘belonging to Brahmā’); subject
indeclinable, conjunctive particle; links this action to Kālī’s in 8.32
√कृ (tanādi, 8U ‘to do, make’), laṅ (imperfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
m. acc. pl. of शत्रु (u-stem); object of अकरोत्
relative pronoun यद्, n. instr. sg., adverbial (‘by which path’)
relative pronoun यद्, n. instr. sg.; the repetition (vīpsā) makes it distributive: ‘wherever’
indeclinable particle; with the present धावति it gives a past meaning
√धाव् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to run’), laṭ (present) with स्म = past, prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada; subject ब्रह्माणी

sandhi.note: a + o → au: हत + ओजस् → हतौजस्.
च + अकरोत् → चाकरोत्. Then the final t, meeting ś, becomes the palatal c, and the ś after it becomes ch: अकरोत् शत्रून् → अकरोच्छत्रून्.

samasa.vigraha: कमण्डलोः जलं कमण्डलुजलम्; तस्य आक्षेपः कमण्डलुजलाक्षेपः; तेन हतं वीर्यं येषां ते, तान्
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣas (कमण्डलुजल, कमण्डलुजलाक्षेप) and a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (…आक्षेपहत)
samasa.literal: those whose valour was struck down by the throwing of water-pot water
samasa.sense: enemies robbed of their strength when Brahmāṇī sprinkled them from her kamaṇḍalu

samasa.literal: those whose vigour is struck down

morph.note: Imperfect of √कृ (stem करो-, augment अ-). With two accusatives — the object शत्रून् and the predicate हतवीर्यान् हतौजसः — it means ‘made (them) such-and-such’.
Present with स्म: a present tense used for a past action, a regular Sanskrit idiom (the particle स्म turns the present into the past). येन येन स्म धावति: ‘wherever she ran’.
Accusative plural of the s-stem adjective हतौजस्; for s-stems the accusative plural has the same form as the nominative plural. It agrees with शत्रून्.

mantras.anvaya: ब्रह्माणी च येन येन धावति स्म, (तत्र) शत्रून् कमण्डलुजलाक्षेपहतवीर्यान् हतौजसः अकरोत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Main clause ब्रह्माणी … शत्रून् … अकरोत् with two predicate accusatives; the relative clause येन येन धावति स्म says where.
mantras.lit: And Brahmāṇī, wherever she ran, made the enemies bereft of valour by the sprinkling of water from her water-pot, bereft of vigour.
mantras.tr: Wherever Brahmāṇī moved, she sprinkled the enemies with water from her water-pot and left them drained of valour and strength.
mantras.tr_note: The compound’s instrument (the sprinkled water) is turned into an action of Brahmāṇī; the sense is unchanged.

comm.t: The Mothers now fight, each with the emblem of the god she came from, as 8.14 announced. Brahmāṇī arrived carrying a rosary and a water-pot (8.15 साक्षसूत्रकमण्डलुः); her weapon is that water-pot. Her water does not wound; it takes the enemy’s strength away.

The hymn of chapter 11 remembers the same act: Brahmāṇī is praised there as the one who sprinkles water with kuśa grass (11.13 कौशाम्भःक्षरिके). The rite-implement of the creator becomes a weapon in the Goddess’s hand.

words.g: f. nom. sg. of माहेश्वरी (taddhita from महेश्वर, with feminine ई); a subject of जघान
n. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); instrument
indeclinable (adverb of manner, here connective)
n. instr. sg. of चक्र; instrument
f. nom. sg. of वैष्णवी (taddhita from विष्णु); a subject of जघान
m. acc. pl. of दैत्य; object of जघान
√हन् (adādi, 2P ‘to strike, kill’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada; construed with each of the three subjects in turn
f. nom. sg. of कौमारी (taddhita from कुमार); a subject of जघान
indeclinable (connective)
f. instr. sg. of शक्ति (i-stem); here the weapon, not the goddess
f. nom. sg. of अतिकोपन; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies कौमारी

sandhi.note: A dental n before the palatal j becomes the palatal nasal ñ.

samasa.vigraha: त्रीणि शूलानि यस्मिन् तत् त्रिशूलम्, तेन
samasa.alt: Also analysed as a samāhāra dvigu (त्रयाणां शूलानां समाहारः), ‘a set of three points’; the bahuvrīhi suits a single weapon better.

samasa.type: prādi tatpuruṣa (karmadhāraya with the prefix अति)

morph.note: Perfect of √हन्: reduplication ज-घान (h becomes gh in the root syllable and j in the reduplication). One singular verb serves three singular subjects, each with her own weapon: ‘Māheśvarī struck … Vaiṣṇavī … Kaumārī …’.
कोपन ‘irascible’ is √कुप् with the agent affix -ana; feminine कोपना. With अति it is an intensive adjective.

mantras.anvaya: माहेश्वरी त्रिशूलेन, तथा वैष्णवी चक्रेण, तथा अतिकोपना कौमारी शक्त्या दैत्यान् जघान।
mantras.anvaya_en: Three subject–instrument pairs share one verb and one object.
mantras.lit: Māheśvarī with the trident, likewise Vaiṣṇavī with the discus, and likewise Kaumārī, exceedingly wrathful, with the spear, struck down the Daityas.
mantras.tr: Māheśvarī struck the Daityas down with her trident, Vaiṣṇavī with her discus, and Kaumārī, blazing with anger, with her spear.

comm.t: Three more Mothers fight, each with her god’s weapon: Śiva’s trident, Viṣṇu’s discus, Skanda’s spear (the śakti Kaumārī held in 8.17, शक्तिहस्ता).

The word शक्ति is used here in its weapon sense — the spear of Skanda — beside its other sense, ‘power’, in which the Mothers themselves are the gods’ śaktis (8.13). The text keeps both meanings in play.

words.en: by the fall of Aindrī’s thunderbolt
words.g: m. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); instrument with विदारिताः
indeclinable (taddhita -शस्, distributive)
m. nom. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); subject of पेतुः
√पत् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to fall’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana, parasmaipada
वि + √दॄ (causative दारि- ‘to tear’) + क्त (past passive participle), m. nom. pl.; qualifies दैत्यदानवाः
f. loc. sg. of पृथ्वी
m. nom. pl. of रुधिरौघप्रवर्षिन्; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies दैत्यदानवाः

sandhi.note: -aḥ before a voiced consonant (here d) becomes -o.
After a vowel other than a/ā, the visarga is sounded r before a voiced consonant.

samasa.vigraha: ऐन्द्र्याः कुलिशम् ऐन्द्रीकुलिशम्; तस्य पातः, तेन
samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: by the falling of Aindrī’s thunderbolt
samasa.sense: under the strokes of Aindrī’s vajra
the asura hosts of both clans (sons of Diti and of Danu)

samasa.vigraha: रुधिरस्य ओघः रुधिरौघः; रुधिरौघं प्रवर्षन्ति इति रुधिरौघप्रवर्षिणः
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (रुधिरौघ)
samasa.sense: streaming with blood as they fell

morph.note: Perfect of √पत् formed without a reduplicated syllable: the root vowel becomes e (पेत्-), as in पेतुः ‘they fell’, नेशुः ‘they vanished’ (8.39).
Past passive participle of the causative वि + √दॄ (दारय-): ‘made to burst, torn open’.

mantras.anvaya: ऐन्द्रीकुलिशपातेन विदारिताः रुधिरौघप्रवर्षिणः दैत्यदानवाः शतशः पृथ्व्यां पेतुः।
mantras.lit: By the fall of Aindrī’s thunderbolt Daityas and Dānavas, torn apart, fell by hundreds on the earth, raining torrents of blood.
mantras.tr: Torn apart by the strokes of Aindrī’s thunderbolt, Daityas and Dānavas fell to the earth in their hundreds, pouring out streams of blood.

comm.t: Aindrī, Indra’s power, who came holding the thunderbolt and riding the king of elephants (8.21), strikes with the vajra. The streams of blood prepare the next episode: Raktabīja, whose every drop of blood will become an asura.
The chapter 11 hymn praises Aindrī as the one with the great thunderbolt who took the life of Vṛtra (11.19 महावज्रे … वृत्रप्राणहरे). Her weapon is Indra’s, and so is her history.

words.en: shattered by blows of the snout
words.g: m. nom. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies the understood subject (the asuras)

words.en: their chests wounded by the tips of the tusks
words.g: m. nom. pl. of the bahuvrīhi stem दंष्ट्राग्रक्षतवक्षस्; compound (see Samāsa)

words.en: by the one in boar form, Vārāhī
words.g: f. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); agent of the participles
नि + √पत् (bhvādi, 1P), laṅ (imperfect), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana, parasmaipada
n. instr. sg. of चक्र; instrument with विदारिताः
indeclinable, conjunctive particle
वि + √दॄ (causative) + क्त, m. nom. pl.

sandhi.note: -āḥ before a voiced consonant loses its visarga.
Final n before c becomes anusvāra + ś: न्यपतन् चक्रेण → न्यपतंश्चक्रेण.
The i of नि becomes y before the augment अ-.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (तुण्डप्रहार)
samasa.literal: destroyed by the blow of the snout

samasa.vigraha: दंष्ट्रायाः अग्रं दंष्ट्राग्रम्; दंष्ट्राग्रेण क्षतं वक्षः येषां ते
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (दंष्ट्राग्र) and a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (…क्षत)
samasa.literal: those whose chests are wounded by the tusk-tip

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (the feminine adjective takes its masculine form as first member)
samasa.sense: by Vārāhī, the power of the Boar
samasa.alt: Or bahuvrīhi: वाराही मूर्तिः यस्याः सा, तया — ‘by her whose form is the boar’s’. Either way the agent is Vārāhī.

morph.note: Imperfect of नि + √पत्: the augment अ- stands between the prefix and the root (नि-अ-पतन्), so the prefix’s i turns to y.
A bahuvrīhi ending in the s-stem वक्षस् ‘chest’: nominative plural -वक्षसः, ‘(those) whose chests …’.

mantras.anvaya: वाराहमूर्त्या तुण्डप्रहारविध्वस्ताः दंष्ट्राग्रक्षतवक्षसः चक्रेण च विदारिताः (असुराः) न्यपतन्।
mantras.anvaya_en: The subject (the asuras) is understood; three descriptions in the nominative plural, all with the agent वाराहमूर्त्या, lead to the verb न्यपतन्.
mantras.lit: Shattered by blows of the snout, their chests wounded by the tips of the tusks, and torn apart by the discus, by the one in boar form, (the asuras) fell.
mantras.tr: Shattered by the blows of her snout, their chests gored by the tips of her tusks, torn apart by her discus, the asuras fell before Vārāhī.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Her’ is supplied: all three weapons are taken as Vārāhī’s (see Commentary).

comm.t: Vārāhī, who came in the form of the sacrificial Boar (8.19), fights as a boar: snout and tusks. The discus in the same sentence is most naturally hers too, though Vaiṣṇavī has just used a discus in 8.34.
The chapter 11 hymn gives the boar-formed Goddess a great discus and the tusk that lifted the earth (11.17 गृहीतोग्रमहाचक्रे दंष्ट्रोद्धृतवसुंधरे), which supports reading the discus here as Vārāhī’s.

words.g: m. instr. pl. of नख; instrument with विदारितान्
वि + √दॄ (causative) + क्त, m. acc. pl.; qualifies महासुरान्
indeclinable, conjunctive particle; links this to the preceding verse
pronominal adjective अन्य, m. acc. pl.; qualifies महासुरान्
√भक्ष् (curādi, 10 ‘to eat’) + शतृ (present participle), f. nom. sg.; qualifies नारसिंही
m. acc. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); object of भक्षयन्ती

words.en: Nārasiṃhī, the power of the Man-Lion
words.g: f. nom. sg. of नारसिंही (taddhita from नरसिंह); subject
√चर् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to move’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
m. loc. sg. of आजि (i-stem)

words.en: she who filled the quarters and the sky with her roar
words.g: f. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies नारसिंही

sandhi.type: visarga sandhi; consonant sandhi (n + c); vowel sandhi
sandhi.note: नखैः before v is sounded नखैर्; विदारितान् before च becomes विदारितांश्; च + अन्यान् → चान्यान्.
a + ā → ā. Further on, दिक् + अम्बर → दिगम्बर: a final stop is voiced before a vowel (झलां जशोऽन्ते, 8.2.39).

samasa.vigraha: दिशश्च अम्बरं च दिगम्बरम्; नादेन आपूर्णं दिगम्बरं यया सा
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (नादापूर्ण) and a samāhāra dvandva (दिगम्बर)
samasa.literal: she by whom the quarters and sky are filled with roaring
samasa.sense: her roars filled every direction and the heavens

morph.note: Present participle of √भक्ष् (stem भक्षय-), feminine in -ई with the nasal: भक्षयन्ती ‘devouring’. It governs the accusative महासुरान्.
Perfect of √चर्, reduplicated च-चार: ‘she moved about’.
Locative singular of the i-stem आजि ‘contest, battle’: -इ + locative → -औ.

Read as one bahuvrīhi: ‘(she) by whom quarters-and-sky were filled with roaring’. Its last members, taken alone, would spell दिगम्बरा ‘sky-clad’, an epithet used elsewhere of Kālī; that is not the sense here.

mantras.anvaya: नादापूर्णदिगम्बरा नारसिंही च नखैः विदारितान् अन्यान् महासुरान् भक्षयन्ती आजौ चचार।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject नारसिंही with her epithet; the participle phrase भक्षयन्ती with its object; the verb चचार with its place आजौ.
mantras.lit: And devouring other great asuras torn apart by her claws, Nārasiṃhī, who filled the quarters and the sky with her roar, roamed in the battle.
mantras.tr: Nārasiṃhī ranged over the field, filling the quarters and the sky with her roar, tearing other great asuras with her claws and devouring them.
mantras.tr_note: The participle विदारितान् (‘torn’) is rendered as a second action of Nārasiṃhī; the Sanskrit makes the asuras the object of one verb, भक्षयन्ती.

comm.t: Nārasiṃhī, who came in a body like the Man-Lion’s, scattering the stars with a toss of her mane (8.20), fights as a lion fights: with claws, teeth and roar. ‘Other’ (अन्यान्) sets her victims apart from those Vārāhī has just struck.

The chapter 11 hymn remembers her as the Goddess in the fierce Man-Lion form who set herself to kill the Daityas (11.18 नृसिंहरूपेणोग्रेण हन्तुं दैत्यान् कृतोद्यमे). Here, as in the hymn, she is named only by her form.

flags.uncertain: अन्यान् can also be read apart from विदारितान् — ‘(those) torn by her claws, and others too’, both devoured. The sense differs little; the reading of the text is not in doubt.
